title: The shape of the heartbeat scatter: Poincare SD1/SD2 HRV, checked against NeuroKit2 and an independent implementation

dataset.name: Fantasia Database
dataset.record: subject f1y01 (young), first 5-min RR window (391 intervals); young-vs-old panel uses all 10 subjects (5 young + 5 old)
dataset.citation: Iyengar N, Peng CK, Morin R, Goldberger AL, Lipsitz LA. Age-related alterations in the fractal scaling of cardiac interbeat interval dynamics. Am J Physiol 1996;271(4):R1078-R1084. Fantasia Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: The sibling HRV-DFA case measured the FRACTAL scaling of the heartbeat (alpha1) and its rise with age. The Poincare plot measures the same heart-rate variability GEOMETRICALLY: plot each RR interval against the next, and the scatter's two axes are SD1 (short-term, beat-to-beat variability, a parasympathetic proxy) and SD2 (long-term variability). On a real 5-minute RR window, ecgHRVpoincare's SD1/SD2 reproduce an independent from-scratch numpy analytical closed-form BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| 0), and NeuroKit2 hrv_nonlinear: SD1 bit-for-bit (SD1 = SDSD/sqrt(2) is universal); SD2 up to a documented ~0.2 ms convention (the op uses the analytical closed-form, NeuroKit2 the geometric paired-projection, which an independent numpy paired projection reproduces bit-for-bit). And the finding: short-term HRV (SD1) is far higher in the young (53.1 ms) than the old (35.3 ms) -- an age-related decline in cardiac-vagal variability, the geometric complement of the DFA aging result.

claims.statement: Poincare SD1 (f1y01, 5-min) -- short-term/beat-to-beat RR variability, a parasympathetic proxy (ms)
Poincare SD2 -- long-term RR variability, analytical closed-form (ms)
SD1/SD2 ratio -- the Poincare cloud's short-to-long axis ratio
max |ecgHRVpoincare - independent numpy analytical closed-form| over SD1/SD2/ratio (bit-exact)
|ecgHRVpoincare SD1 - NeuroKit2 SD1| -- bit-exact (SD1 = universal SDSD/sqrt(2))
|independent numpy paired-projection SD2 - NeuroKit2 SD2| -- bit-exact (identifies NeuroKit2's SD2 convention)
|op SD2 (analytical closed-form) - NeuroKit2 SD2 (paired projection)| -- a documented ~0.2 ms convention gap
mean Poincare SD1 across the 5 young subjects (short-term HRV)
mean Poincare SD1 across the 5 old subjects -- markedly lower (age-related vagal decline)

validation.reference: ecgHRVpoincare (Brennan et al. 2001 closed-form, R unbiased n-1 variance) is validated three ways, all exact. (1) An independent from-scratch numpy implementation of the op's OWN analytical closed-form (SD1 = sqrt(0.5*var(diff RR)), SD2 = sqrt(2*SDNN^2 - 0.5*SDSD^2)) reproduces SD1/SD2/ratio BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| = 0). (2) NeuroKit2 hrv_nonlinear's SD1 equals the op's SD1 BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| = 0) -- SD1 = SDSD/sqrt(2) is the universal definition. (3) NeuroKit2's SD2 is the GEOMETRIC paired-projection std((RR_n+RR_n+1)/sqrt(2)); an independent numpy paired projection reproduces NeuroKit2's SD2 BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| = 0), so the only op-vs-NeuroKit2 SD2 gap (~0.196 ms, ~0.24%) is a documented convention choice (analytical closed-form vs paired projection), not an error. Peaks are reconstructed from the integer-ms RR at 250 Hz so NeuroKit2 sees the IDENTICAL RR. The finding: SD1 declines with age (young 53.1 -> old 35.3 ms).
validation.data: REAL -- Fantasia (PhysioNet), subject f1y01 (young) 5-min RR for the certified op; all 10 subjects (5 young + 5 old) for the aging panel
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) ecgHRVpoincare reproduces an independent numpy analytical closed-form bit-for-bit (max |diff| 0), its SD1 equals NeuroKit2's SD1 bit-for-bit, and NeuroKit2's SD2 equals an independent numpy paired projection bit-for-bit; (2) short-term HRV (SD1) is far higher in the young (53.1 ms) than the old (35.3 ms). HONEST scope: (1) this is a genuine MACHINE-PRECISION cross-tool match -- the op and the independent numpy compute the IDENTICAL analytical closed-form, so the max |diff| = 0 is exact, not a convention agreement; (2) SD1 matches NeuroKit2 bit-for-bit because SD1 = SDSD/sqrt(2) is universal; the op-vs-NeuroKit2 SD2 gap (~0.196 ms) is purely a CONVENTION difference -- the op uses the Brennan analytical closed-form (full-series SDNN identity), NeuroKit2 the geometric paired-projection (drops the last point), which an independent numpy paired projection reproduces bit-for-bit; both are standard and equivalent in the large-n limit, so neither is wrong; (3) the aging finding -- SD1 higher in young -- is a descriptive cardiac-autonomic pattern on n=5 young + 5 old, one database, the geometric complement of the DFA aging result (alpha1 rises with age) on the same cohort, NOT a clinical claim; (4) a 5-min window (Task Force short-term HRV) of one subject for the certified op; run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic closed form).

open_questions.q: The op reports SD1/SD2 (the standard descriptors); the full Poincare literature adds the higher-order and complex descriptors (SD1/SD2 area, the complex correlation measure, and the temporal asymmetry / Guzik & Porta indices that separate heart-rate decelerations from accelerations). Computing the asymmetry indices across the young/old cohort -- and pairing them with the DFA alpha1 on the same beats -- would test whether the geometric and fractal aging signatures track the same autonomic change. Documented, not escalated.

reference_tools: independent numpy Poincare closed-form + paired projection (Python)
